title: islanded-region-eviction-and-backpressure-slo-hotfix
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: following a partial network partition incident in us-west-2 we observed an 'islanded region' pattern where a subset of nodes continued accepting requests but lost connectivity to our global control plane and downstream KV cache. Two issues made this worse: 1) the region-level circuit breaker failed to open quickly when loss of heartbeats coincided with aggressive KV cache eviction, and 2) tenant-level SLO budgets were not being re-provisioned to reflect sudden capacity loss, causing high-priority traffic to be starved by background low-priority workloads. This PR implements a fast-path isolation policy that: (a) detects islanded-region semantics (heartbeat delta + cache-thrash signal) and flips an emergency backpressure marker; (b) triggers prioritized eviction of best-effort requests and request-level early-exit with HTTP 429 for low-priority routes; (c) updates the SLO enforcer to re-weight token budgets immediately under emergency backpressure; and (d) fixes a race in the region circuit-breaker where repeated KV cache invalidations could prevent Open->Closed transitions. Changes are conservative and opt-in behind a feature flag `islanded_fastpath_v1` for staged rollout. Design notes: - Detection: combine node heartbeat loss (>3s missed) with cache-thrash metric (kv_evictions_per_sec > threshold) to avoid false positives during short control-plane jitter. - Eviction semantics: best-effort routes are drained first; streaming/chat sessions are checkpointed and offered a graceful close signal; high-priority inference (reserved/dedicated customers) keep their token budgets but may experience slightly higher latency due to FQ backpressure. - SLO enforcer: when backpressure marker is set, tenant token allocations are scaled by emergency_factor (default 0.5) except for pinned tenants (matches dedicated/reserved mapping). - Circuit-breaker fix: avoid a missed-open path by making state transitions idempotent and introducing an in-memory 'pending_open' set persisted to raft-config for 10s to survive quick flaps. Testing & rollout: - Unit tests for detector heuristics and SLO re-weighting added. - Local chaos tests simulate control-plane partition with simulated KV thrash. - Canary rollout: start feature flag on staging, then route 5% of us-west-2 traffic to the new path; increase to 50% if metrics show reduced P95 degradation. Observability: new metrics exported: islanded_backpressure_active (0/1), islanded_evict_rate, islanded_slo_scale_factor; dashboards and alerting rules added in observability-pack. Risk & mitigation: false positives could evict unnecessarily; mitigated by dual-signal detection and feature flag. Rollback via disabling `islanded_fastpath_v1` or setting emergency_factor=1. Related: incident SUP-987, ENG-2120.

release_notes: - Fix: region circuit-breaker missed-open race causing islanded regions to continue accepting traffic under control-plane partition; now durable for short flaps. - Feature: emergency backpressure path that prioritizes eviction of best-effort requests and reweights tenant SLO budgets under islanded-region conditions. - Telemetry: new islanded_backpressure_active, islanded_evict_rate, islanded_slo_scale_factor metrics
notes_for_oncall: If you see islanded_backpressure_active=1 in us-west-2: check detector thresholds and kv_evictions_per_sec; quick mitigation is to disable feature flag `islanded_fastpath_v1` or set emergency_factor=1. For persistent control-plane instability, escalate SUP-987.
